title: The system: an online shop, balanced at every tier
caption: DNS picks the region, L4 spreads connections, L7 routes requests by path; every service behind it is a stateless pool.

steps.text: The browser resolves shop.com. GeoDNS answers with the virtual IP (VIP) of the nearest healthy region, with a short TTL (30–60 s).
The L4 load balancer owns that VIP. It never reads HTTP: it hashes each TCP connection (source/dest IP and port) to one L7 proxy, at millions of connections per second.
The L7 proxies terminate TLS and read the request: / and /product/* go to the web pool, /api/cart/* to checkout, /api/search to search.
Inside each pool the proxy picks an instance by least outstanding requests, and health checks every few seconds keep sick instances out of rotation.
Services are stateless: carts and logins live in the session store and orders in the database, so any instance can serve any request.
A second region runs the same stack. The GSLB health-checks both and can move users there in about a minute.

scenarios.name: Flash sale
scenarios.summary: 10× traffic in a minute: L4 barely notices, the L7 pool and checkout autoscale, and least-requests keeps new instances from being flooded.

steps.text: A sale starts: requests jump from 5 000/s to 50 000/s within a minute.
L4 forwards packets and has headroom; the L7 pool scales out on CPU (TLS handshakes are the cost).
Checkout autoscales. New instances get a slow start so cold caches aren't hit with full load at once.
The session store and DB are the real limit: the proxy sheds /api/search first to protect checkout.

scenarios.name: Region A outage
scenarios.summary: The whole region fails: GSLB health checks notice and DNS points users at region B. Recovery is bounded by the DNS TTL.

steps.text: A power failure takes out region A's load balancers.
The GSLB's health checks to region A's VIP fail three times in a row (~30 s).
DNS now answers with region B's VIP; users move as their cached answer expires.
Region B takes double load: it must be sized for it, and its database must be a promoted replica.

scenarios.name: Rolling deploy
scenarios.summary: Ship checkout v2 with zero errors: drain an instance, upgrade, health-check it back in, repeat. The load balancer is what makes this safe.

steps.text: Mark one checkout instance as draining: the proxy sends it no new requests.
In-flight requests finish (up to a 30 s drain timeout), then the instance is upgraded.
Passing health checks re-admit it with slow start; repeat for the next instance.
Sessions are in the session store, so no shopper loses a cart.
